subproblem.title: Two-sided local sup-norm bound for g ↦ ∫_{E∩U} div g from locally finite perimeter
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N open and E ⊆ ℝ^N Lebesgue null-measurable, and suppose E has locally finite perimeter in U (SimonGMT IsLocallyBV U χ_E). Then for every compact K ⊆ U there is a constant C ≥ 0 with the following property. For every C¹ map g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ K, and every M ∈ ℝ with |g(x)| ≤ M for all x ∈ ℝ^N, we have |∫_{E∩U} div g dL^N| ≤ C · M.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U E : Set (Rn N)), IsOpen U → NullMeasurableSet E volume → HasLocallyFinitePerimeter U E → ∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ g : Rn N → Rn N, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ K → ∀ M : ℝ, (∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ M) → |∫ x in E ∩ U, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g x| ≤ C * M
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 0, 2 and 3 of the parent proof, together with remark (R1) of the gauss_green proof ("if g is C¹ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U then div g = 0 off tsupport g, so ∫_{E∩U} div g = ∫_W χ_E div g"). Underlying text: Simon Ch. 2, (2.1) and the remark after it (chapter-02.txt lines 480-498, printed p. 48), applied to u = χ_E as in Simon Ch. 3, §4 (chapter-03.txt lines 555-573). The bound "c(W) sup|g|" is stated here with an arbitrary upper bound M for |g|.

Notation. χ_E = E.indicator 1, and div g = trace of Dg (SimonGMT euclideanDivergence). By definition, HasLocallyFinitePerimeter U E is IsLocallyBV U χ_E. That is: U is open; χ_E is locally integrable on U; and for every open W with closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U (IsRelativelyCompactIn W U) there is c ≥ 0 such that ∫_W χ_E(x) div G(x) dx ≤ c · compactlySupportedSupNorm G for every G ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ^N) that is C¹ (IsC1TestField G) and has tsupport G ⊆ W. Here compactlySupportedSupNorm G = sSup {|G(x)| : x ∈ ℝ^N}.

1. Choice of W and C. Let K ⊆ U be compact. Since ℝ^N is locally compact and regular and U is open, there is an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U (Mathlib exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure). Thus W ⊂⊂ U, and the third component of the BV hypothesis, applied to W, gives c ≥ 0 as above. Put C := c ≥ 0. It depends only on K, through W.

2. One-sided bound. Claim: if g is C¹ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ K, and |g(x)| ≤ M for all x, then ∫_{E∩U} div g ≤ c·M.
 (a) Let G ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ^N) be g bundled with its continuity (g is C¹, hence continuous) and its compact support; as a function, G = g. Then G is a C¹ test field and tsupport G = tsupport g ⊆ K ⊆ W. By step 1, ∫_W χ_E div g ≤ c · compactlySupportedSupNorm G.
 (b) (R1): ∫_W χ_E div g = ∫_{E∩U} div g. Put f := div g. By SimonGMT support_euclideanDivergence_subset, f(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport g, in particular for x ∉ W. For all x, χ_E(x) f(x) = (E.indicator f)(x). Since W is open, hence measurable, ∫_W E.indicator f = ∫_{ℝ^N} W.indicator(E.indicator f) (integral_indicator). Pointwise, W.indicator(E.indicator f) = (E ∩ U).indicator f. If x ∈ W, then x ∈ U (because W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U), and both sides equal 1_E(x) f(x). If x ∉ W, the left side is 0, and so is the right side, since f(x) = 0. Finally, E ∩ U is null-measurable (E is null-measurable and U is open, hence measurable). So ∫_{ℝ^N} (E ∩ U).indicator f = ∫_{E∩U} f (integral_indicator₀). These are equalities of integrands and integrals and need no integrability assumption.
 (c) compactlySupportedSupNorm G ≤ M. The set {|g(x)| : x ∈ ℝ^N} is nonempty (ℝ^N ≠ ∅), and each of its elements is ≤ M, so its supremum is ≤ M (csSup_le).
 (d) Combining (a)-(c) with c ≥ 0: ∫_{E∩U} div g = ∫_W χ_E div g ≤ c · compactlySupportedSupNorm G ≤ c·M.

3. The lower bound. Let g and M be as in step 2. Then −g is C¹ with compact support, tsupport(−g) = tsupport g ⊆ K, and |(−g)(x)| = |g(x)| ≤ M. By step 2, ∫_{E∩U} div(−g) ≤ c·M. For every x, D(−g)(x) = −Dg(x) (fderiv_neg, which needs no differentiability hypothesis), and the trace is linear, so div(−g) = −div g pointwise. Hence ∫_{E∩U} div(−g) = −∫_{E∩U} div g (integral_neg), and therefore −∫_{E∩U} div g ≤ c·M.

4. Conclusion. Steps 2 and 3 give −c·M ≤ ∫_{E∩U} div g ≤ c·M, i.e. |∫_{E∩U} div g| ≤ C·M with C = c ≥ 0. Since C was chosen in step 1 before g and M, it satisfies the statement for the given compact K. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose an open W with K ⊆ W and closure W compact ⊆ U; the IsLocallyBV hypothesis for W gives c ≥ 0, and C := c.
(R1): for C¹ g supported in K, ∫_W χ_E div g = ∫_{E∩U} div g, because div g vanishes off tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U and E ∩ U is null-measurable.
compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≤ M, so ∫_{E∩U} div g ≤ c M.
Apply this to −g, using div(−g) = −div g, to get the lower bound; hence |∫_{E∩U} div g| ≤ C M.
